text:
maya: noticed repeated OOMs on prod-worker-24 around 02:10-02:40 UTC, correlated with long-context customer sessions (~150k tokens). stack traces point to kv cache growth, not GPU OOM.
liam: can you paste the logs?
maya: paste of relevant logs:
```
[2025-03-08T02:12:11Z] runtime: alloc failed: requested 1.2GB, available 48MB -> kv_cache_alloc.cpp:214
[2025-03-08T02:12:11Z] trace: prefix_len=124800 tokens, reuse_hits=0.35, evict_attempts=3, page_count=18
[2025-03-08T02:12:11Z] fallback: routed to model-small-quant-v2
```
maya: also see sharp increase in pagewalks in perf profile (flamegraph attached to perf dashboard) -> https://internal.redwood/dashboards/kv/paging?run=174560
anya: saw the alert, was oncall. Triage notes: paging spiked after a new customer started a 4-hour session with nested tool calls. KV reuse wasn't effective because the prefix shapes changed frequently.
noah: do we have repro? liam: I reproduced with local runner on a 40k token trace by looping tool calls; memory climbs steadily even when tokens stop growing — looks like fragmentation + sticky slabs.
liam: quick profiling snippet:
```
# kv sampler
sample 0: slab0 64MB used, free 12MB
sample 100: slab0 64MB used, free 2MB, free_frag 9MB
sample 300: slab0 64MB used, free 0MB -> evict fails (soft)
```
maya: that matches prod. hypothesis: reuse window logic keeps references to many small KV entries (per-tool state) preventing coalescing and causing slab fragmentation. paging then tries to spill and thrashes.
anya: immediate mitigation suggestion: reduce reuse window from 15m -> 2m for hosted tier 3, enable aggressive soft-evict for entries < 1k tokens.
noah: agree. also add a KV-page backoff: if page_count > 10 in 30s, stop prefetch and bias to eviction.
liam: small config patch I tried locally seemed promising:
```
{ "kv": { "reuse_window_ms": 120000, "aggressive_soft_evict_threshold_tokens": 1024, "page_backoff_threshold": 10 } }
```
liam: with that, steady-state memory drop ~22% and maximum resident set 18% lower in the repro. latency p95 unaffected for short requests.
maya: can we roll this as a 10% canary to hosted for 1 hour? ops-bot: deploy request queued.
ops-bot: deploy started: canary group prod-hosted-1 (10%) -> deploy id d-174560-01
anya: watch the OOM alerts and `kv.pagewalk.ops` metric. Also add a short-term alert for sustained `kv.evictions.failed > 5` in 5m.
noah: long-term: we should improve slab coalescing and add a reuse TTL per-key rather than global reuse window. Also consider compaction during low-load windows.
liam: notebook profiling shows fragmentation hotspots in allocator path when there are many small variable-length KV entries. I'll write a microbenchmark to reproduce fragmentation pattern.
maya: curious: kernel selection changes last week — any chance different kernels cause different allocation patterns?
liam: good point. I compared kernels: new attention kernel uses different allocation stride causing slightly different alignment -> increases external fragmentation by ~4%. Not the main cause but amplifies it.
anya: next actions:
- canary the config change (maya, liam, ops)
- add temporary alert (anya)
- liam to land microbenchmark and proposed allocator coalesce PR
- noah to draft long-term compaction/playbook
maya: also create fallback policy: when kv.evictions.failed > 5 and memory > 80% of heap, route sessions to model-small-quant-v2 and mark session as "degraded but alive". We should surface to customer as rate-limited fallbacks.
noah: I'll draft customer-facing fallback wording.
liam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7823 (draft) — contains reuse_window toggle + backoff metric.
ops-bot: canary deployment complete: d-174560-01 -> success (10%): 1745603620
maya: early signal: canary nodes showed 20% fewer pagewalks and no OOMs in that hour.
anya: rolling to 100% in 30m if no regressions.
liam: will also instrument per-key reuse TTLs in next patch, but that needs schema change.
maya: thanks everyone. document findings in incident tracker and add to runbook under "kv-fragmentation".
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2025-0364, severity: medium, owner: anya
noah: adding notes to postmortem template.
maya: closing thread after roll to 100% and followups. :thumbsup:
